findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false but still dereferences feature flag
findings.body: pkg/expr/reader.go: enableSqlExpressions computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)` then returns false on both branches. Since the intent is to unconditionally disable SQL expressions, it should just return false. As written it needlessly dereferences h/h.features, so a nil reader or nil FeatureToggles panics instead of returning the safe 'not implemented' error, turning a blocked query into a crash/DoS, and the inverted negation leaves a trap where a future edit to re-enable will enable when the flag is off.

findings.title: tablesFromAST indexes ast[0] without length check
findings.body: pkg/expr/sql/parser.go: tablesFromAST does `flatten.Flatten(ast[0], ...)` with no check that ast is non-empty. A JSON payload of `[]` (e.g. empty result from RunCommands / json_serialize_sql) causes an index-out-of-range panic, crashing the query path. Caller TablesList only checks json.Unmarshal error, not len(ast)==0, so an attacker-controlled SQL string that serializes to an empty array causes DoS.

findings.title: NoData result immediately overwritten by TableData
findings.body: pkg/expr/sql_command.go: Execute sets `rsp.Values = NoData{Frame}` when `frame.Rows()==0` then unconditionally overwrites it on the next lines with `rsp.Values = TableData{Frame}`. The NoData branch is dead, so empty SQL results are never reported as NoData, breaking downstream no-data/alerting semantics.
